headline: Norway's government plans to propose a temporary ban on AI-equipped glasses in selected public places over privacy concerns.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a proposal only, but an early government move on camera glasses.
importance_line: People in public spaces, schools and changing areas gain possible protection from being filmed without knowing, while makers of smart glasses face limits; it is only a proposal and parliament has not voted.
summary: Reuters reports, as carried by Livemint, that Norway's government said on 5 Oct 2026 it will propose a temporary ban on AI glasses in selected places such as parks, beaches, museums, schools and gyms with changing rooms, because people could be filmed or recorded without knowing. It is not a total ban, private use would stay allowed, and a bill is to go to parliament as soon as possible.
notes: Read at Livemint carrying Reuters; Reuters is credited.
